lessons.title: Field paths were checked last cycle, enum SEMANTICS were not
lessons.detail: v3.1.0 verified that `vatType` exists and is required, then documented it as '0 before VAT / 1 included' at both levels. The spec's DocumentVatType and ItemVatType are different enums: at document level 1 means EXEMPT. The skill told builders to choose 1 at document level for a VAT-inclusive sale, which issues an osek murshe document as VAT-exempt with no API error. Extending last cycle's lesson: for every enum the skill names, read the enum's value table in the spec, per schema, not once per field name.

lessons.title: A gateway cannot be called 'undocumented' from a section inventory
lessons.detail: Tranzila (Notify URL, notify_url_address) and Grow (developers.grow.business Webhooks service) both publish their callback mechanism; the prior cycles concluded 'no webhook page' / 'no resolvable developer host' from a navigation list and a dead hostname. Search the vendor's sitemap.xml and the renamed developer host before declaring a payload unverifiable.

lessons.title: Plan availability needs the premium-app rule, not a help-article banner
lessons.detail: Webhooks by Zapier was stated as 'available on all plans' because help articles carry a generic 'Available on plans: Free ...' banner. The app is Premium and premium apps are paid-only, which made every webhook recipe in the skill impossible on Free. Check the app page's Premium tag and the pricing table row.

lessons.title: Code snippets in references are scripts
lessons.detail: The Template 7 VAT-summary code treated Morning's `amount` (total INCLUDING VAT) as pre-VAT revenue and then added VAT again, and the phone formatter turned 054-123-4567 into +97254-123-4567. Both ran without error. Execute every inline code block with realistic, messy inputs, and check each field's meaning in the vendor schema before trusting the arithmetic.

persistent_fail.title: Evidence gate passed on snippets echoed from the claim, not fetched from the source
persistent_fail.detail: Two fabricated or long-dead claims survived the v2.2.0 gate because their raw_snippet was derived from the claim text rather than from fetched page content. 'zapier-pricing-tiers-2026' asserted a Starter plan discontinued in April 2024 on the strength of raw_snippet 'Starter ... Professional'. 'green-invoice-mcp-link' asserted a directory listing that has never existed on the strength of raw_snippet 'green-invoice-mcp'. A one-or-two-token snippet that is a substring of the claim proves nothing. Future gates should reject any raw_snippet that is fully contained in the claim text, and should require a snippet long enough to be falsifiable.

persistent_fail.title: Troubleshooting sections can entrench a wrong mechanism
persistent_fail.detail: The Cardcom IndicatorUrl/GET/DealResponse error was not merely stated once; the Troubleshooting entry for 'Webhook not receiving data from Cardcom' instructed the reader to verify the IndicatorUrl, confirm production mode, and check that Catch Hook accepts GET. Every one of those steps pushes a user further from the real cause. When correcting a mechanism, always grep the Troubleshooting and Gotchas blocks for the same mechanism, not just the instructional steps.

persistent_fail.title: One dead source URL backing a multi-vendor table
persistent_fail.detail: A single evidence claim ('decimal-shekels-israeli-processors') sourced payload and unit claims for six separate vendors to one Cardcom KB URL, which now returns 523. Only the Cardcom portion was ever verifiable from that source. Per-vendor claims need per-vendor sources; where no public spec exists (Grow by Meshulam), the skill must say 'unverified' rather than assert field names.

persistent_fail.title: Third-party platform drift outran the review interval
persistent_fail.detail: Between v2.2.0 (2026-05-20) and this review, Zapier's plan lineup, WhatsApp app surface, app count and Israeli-vendor app coverage all moved, and Cardcom's documented webhook mechanism turned out to have been wrong since creation rather than drifted. For platform-wrapper skills, verify vendor API shape against a machine-readable spec (OpenAPI/swagger JSON) rather than a KB article: the spec is greppable, self-dating, and lets you prove a field name is ABSENT, which prose cannot.

persistent_fail.title: Four CRITICAL API-shape defects survived every prior gate because the gates check values, not field paths
persistent_fail.detail: The published v3.0.1 told builders to map a Cardcom top-level `Amount` (the callback has none; it is TranzactionInfo.Amount), to send Morning `items[].unitPrice` (the schema is income[].price and has no items property), to read the allocation number off the create-document response (it is not there; allocationNumber is on the Document schema), and never mentioned that the Morning token expires in one hour, so no recipe fetched one. Every fact-freshness and rate-table gate passed, because each checks whether a stated VALUE is current, not whether a stated FIELD PATH exists in the vendor schema. The fix that generalises: for any skill that maps vendor payloads, fetch the OpenAPI/JSON spec and assert every field path the skill names actually exists in the named schema, and that required-field lists are complete. A field path is falsifiable cheaply and mechanically; nothing in the pipeline was doing it.

persistent_fail.title: A reviewer finding is a lead, not a fact, in both directions
persistent_fail.detail: The Independent Judge reported the WhatsApp Notifications 'only messages your own number' claim as unsourced, having checked the app directory page. Acting on it would have weakened a correct, well-sourced statement: Zapier's help article (updated 2026-05-29) says verbatim 'send yourself WhatsApp messages to your WhatsApp account', lists the seven prefilled templates and states 'Custom templates cannot be created'. The claim was restored and strengthened instead. Separately the judge proposed 'correcting' the 67(א2)(1) / 20(ג)(1) citations, which this cycle had just fixed and which are right. Always verify a finding against the primary source before acting, including findings that propose a deletion.

unverified.title: Zapier Central to Agents rename has no citable Zapier statement
unverified.detail: The rename is evidenced only by redirects (zapier.com/central -> /agents, central.zapier.com -> agents.zapier.com). No changelog or announcement stating it was located. The skill now says so explicitly rather than attributing the rename to Zapier.

unverified.title: Cardcom webhook has no signature mechanism we could find
unverified.detail: A grep of the v11 spec found no HMAC, signature or checksum on the callback, so a Catch Hook URL is forgeable. The skill documents mitigations (re-fetch by LowProfileId, echo a secret through ReturnValue) and states this is 'none found in the spec' rather than a guarantee. Confirm with Cardcom support.

unverified.item: Morning payment[] row requirement for type 320
unverified.detail: The spec lists payment[] row required fields but does not state whether a 320 without payment rows is rejected. The skill tells builders to add one; confirm in the sandbox.

unverified.detail: Sourced to Tranzila's own Base44 Notify guide (code sample), not a field reference table. ccno and index left out deliberately.
